ai.heading: Applied AI, engineered like the rest of the system.
ai.intro: Patterns I can point to in the code of each system, not slogans.

principles.d: In CRMA an AI write becomes a proposal that expires after 72 hours unless approved. In Dhura agents emit actions that a person approves before a domain use case runs. In ProspectIQ the approved action is reauthorized at execution time.

CRMA and ProspectIQ run model-directed tool loops: the model picks the next tool from the last result, inside server-side budgets for steps and calls. Dhura deliberately does not: its agents are deterministic.
CRMA fuses lexical and vector results with Reciprocal Rank Fusion, filtered by organization. ProspectIQ mixes keyword and embedding scores, with a local hashing embedding by default.
Dhura routes every model call through a provider-neutral gateway with schema-validated output. Mtjri validates generated store content before it is saved.
Tools, retrieval and generated content are scoped to the same tenant as the rest of the data: by organization in CRMA, by tenant in Dhura, by store in Mtjri.

hirelens.versions: Job and CV versions are frozen per candidate, so the Candidate 360 view stays consistent even when a job changes later.

Prompt-injection and forbidden-decision-language checks on the copilot.

linguacoach.lede: English coaching for Arabic speakers, designed to keep teaching even when no paid AI provider is connected.

runtime: Routes between deterministic dev/test providers and OpenAI, Gemini, Ollama or any OpenAI-compatible endpoint.
A monthly budget and per-user daily limits.
When a provider call is skipped, the result says so. Progress is never invented.
linguacoach.durable: Structured AI workflows are persisted as queued runs and executed by a bounded in-process worker that holds durable PostgreSQL row leases.
linguacoach.realtime: Coaching conversations stream over Server-Sent Events.

prospectiq.title: ProspectIQ
prospectiq.lede: Evidence-grounded B2B research and sales intelligence.
prospectiq.summary: ProspectIQ is an evidence-grounded B2B research and sales intelligence system. It combines multi-source research, deterministic scoring, Evidence Graphs, Delta Intelligence, internal Sales Knowledge retrieval and a bounded model-directed agent runtime. Consequential actions are proposed first, explicitly approved, reauthorized at execution time, executed atomically, audited, and resumed within the same AgentRun.

evidence.d: Every provider result is normalized into claims that carry a source, a time and a confidence. The Evidence Graph resolves those claims into facts, and FactResolver weighs sources with fixed, auditable quality weights: a crawl of the company’s own site outranks a directory listing.
evidence.note: Apify only runs actors the backend allowlists. The model cannot pass an actor ID, and there is no tool for fetching an arbitrary URL.

score.t: The score belongs to the backend
score.d: ICP fit, signals, digital maturity, the score breakdown and deltas are all computed in code. The model interprets the result. It never computes the facts it is interpreting.
score.formulaTitle: Digital maturity, as the code computes it
score.cap: Capped at 100. Low below 40, medium from 40, high from 70.

delta.d: A new research run is compared with the last one, fact by fact. Only a real change in a canonical fact becomes a change event, and its effect on the score is recalculated by the same deterministic rules.
delta.note: The model never decides whether something changed. It can only explain a change the diff engine has already recorded.

knowledge.evidenceQ: What is true about the prospect?
knowledge.evidenceD: Tavily, SerpAPI and Apify research, plus earlier runs.
knowledge.salesQ: What can we credibly sell them?
knowledge.salesD: Services, case studies, playbooks, past proposals and internal docs.
knowledge.noneD: When nothing in the knowledge base fits, the Copilot says so. It does not invent a service to make the answer look better.
knowledge.rag: Sales knowledge lives in MariaDB. Tenancy is filtered inside the query, then cosine similarity runs in Python over a bounded candidate set. The retrieval architecture is sized to the current corpus instead of adding vector infrastructure without a measured need. Retrieved text is always treated as untrusted.

runtime.d: The model picks each tool based on what the previous tool returned. The backend validates the arguments against the tool’s schema, checks workspace and permissions, runs it and hands the result back. The order of calls is never scripted.

classes.d: Lead, evidence, score, history and deltas
Tavily, SerpAPI and allowlisted Apify crawls
Sales knowledge, playbooks and case studies
Notes, follow-ups, tasks, stage, tags and drafts, as previews
Deep-research requests and external sends. Sending is high risk and off by default

runtime.bounds: Server-side budgets cap steps, tool calls, searches, crawls and runtime, and identical repeated calls are blocked. One shared runtime serves every agent profile: research, sales copilot, read-only and admin.

approval.t: AI can propose. The backend executes.
approval.quote: Proposal-time permission is never trusted at execution time.
approval.d: Expired, rejected or tampered actions cannot run, and approving an action that has already executed changes nothing.

resume.d: When the run reaches a consequential action it stops and waits. After the backend confirms the approval, the same AgentRun continues on the same live stream. No new workflow is started.
resume.illustrative: An interactive replay of the lifecycle and its real event names, not a recording of a run.
resume.sse: Live event streaming with persisted replay and reconnect support.

verification.d: Gates as recorded in the repository’s latest release report. Documented there, not rerun for this page; see below for what was executed.

items: mypy strict · 235 source files, no issues

verification.modes: Live, demo and stub modes are explicit, and production fails closed instead of falling back to demo data.

items: Dialogs return focus to the control that opened them
Focus stays trapped inside open dialogs
Copilot, Evidence Graph and Research History are labelled regions
Every select on the lead page has an accessible name
Map markers are named after the company
Live regions stay bounded during a Copilot run
Statuses carry text, not only colour
a11y.note: Audited with axe-core against WCAG 2.1 A and AA on the new surfaces and the lead page. Contrast was checked against the design tokens.

prospectiq.architecture: FastAPI, Pydantic v2, SQLAlchemy 2 and Alembic on MariaDB. Research through Tavily, SerpAPI and allowlisted Apify actors. A single agent runtime with a typed ToolRegistry, an approval gate and live event streaming. A React, TypeScript and Vite frontend, Docker Compose.
verified: A model-directed runtime: the model returns tool calls, the backend validates and runs them, within budgets.
The approval gate checks expiry, workspace membership and a SHA-256 payload hash, then claims the action atomically.
Approval is idempotent, and the same AgentRun resumes after the decision.
Hybrid retrieval of keyword and embedding scores; the default embedding is a local hashing model.
notClaimed: It is not deployed, and has no customers or usage figures.
Retrieval quality has not been benchmarked against a hosted embedding model.
External providers (Tavily, SerpAPI, Apify, model APIs) were not called during this audit.
The release-report figures above were not reproduced here.
prospectiq.tests: Executed on 18 Oct 2026 with SQLite and provider keys blanked: 567 passed, 3 failed, 6 skipped. The 3 failures are production-config checks that require a search API key, which was removed on purpose.

Each business area owns its domain, application and infrastructure code.

tenant_id referenced across hundreds of backend files.

A provider-neutral AI gateway with schema-validated output.

The agents are deterministic, not autonomous.

careerguide.title: CareerGuide AI
careerguide.lede: Career matching for university students where the score is reproducible. AI can advise; it never decides the number.

careerguide.weightsNote: Weights shift only when fresh market evidence exists — and AI or live web search never set a score directly.
careerguide.immutable: Every recommendation version is immutable. A new score means an explicit re-score, not an overwrite.
careerguide.aiTitle: AI beside the engine, not inside it

crma.title: CRMA
crma.lede: A multi-tenant CRM where AI agents propose and people approve.
crma.heroAlt: CRMA copilot paused on a proposed deal stage change, with the field diff, the reason, and Approve and Reject buttons
crma.summary: CRMA is a multi-tenant CRM built on Laravel 12 and React 19. AI agents can search, research and draft, but they can never change data on their own. Every write becomes a proposal with a field-level diff, a stated reason and a risk class, and the agent run pauses until a person approves, edits or rejects it.

facts.v: Repository owner and engineering lead, with AI pair programming
B2B sales CRM in Arabic and English
Web app, versioned REST API and an MCP server

problem: Sales teams want AI help, but a model with write access to shared customer records is a liability. One wrong stage change or outbound message reaches real people.
Most AI features in a CRM either stay read-only and add little, or act on their own and add risk.
Teams in the Gulf need a native Arabic, right-to-left interface, not a translated afterthought.

modules.d: One workspace for the whole pipeline. Every screen here is the running application on seeded demo data.

pipeline.d: Kanban stages with a rule-based health score on every card, and a review strip that counts stale, stuck and unscheduled deals.
pipeline.alt: Deal pipeline with Kanban stages, health scores on each card and the pipeline review strip

deal-workspace.d: Key facts, stage history and next steps, with a health score that lists each rule that cost points.
deal-workspace.alt: Deal workspace with deal health, key facts and next steps

contacts.d: People and companies, scoped to the organisation that owns them.

leads.d: Scored leads from every intake channel, ready to qualify or convert.
leads.alt: Leads list with scores and sources

tasks.d: Follow-ups linked to the deal, lead or contact they belong to.

workflows.d: Automations built in a visual builder and validated before they can go live.

flow.t: How work moves through the system
flow.d: Event-driven. A record change can start a workflow, the AI reads freely, and every write it wants waits for a person.

steps.d: Leads arrive from Meta lead ads, WhatsApp, web forms and CSV import.
Each lead becomes a record with a rule-based score, and every deal carries a health score. The numbers come from CRM data, not from a model.
A record event starts a workflow. The graph is validated before it can be activated, and its expressions use a typed DSL instead of eval().
steps.alt: Workflow builder: trigger, condition, two task branches

steps.d: The copilot reads and searches freely. Anything that would change data becomes a proposal with a diff, a reason and a risk class, and it expires after 72 hours by default.
A person approves, edits or rejects it in the AI Action Center. Only low and medium risk proposals can be approved together.
steps.alt: AI Action Center with two proposals waiting for review

steps.d: Only an approved action runs. The paused agent run then resumes with its context intact, and the proposal moves to its final tab in the Action Center.

arch.d: A modular monolith. Every box maps to code or configuration in the repository.

edge.d: Scoped to a tenant and checked against a policy before any domain code runs.

app.d: Laravel 12 on PHP 8.3, split by domain.

async.d: Queues split by workload, a scheduler and WebSockets.

data.d: One relational store, scoped by organisation.

arch.delivery: Docker Compose services, a GitHub Actions pipeline for tests, lint and deploy, and a release script that switches an atomic symlink and rolls back when the health check fails.

ai.d: The agent runtime pauses the run, shows a field-level diff with the reason and the risk, and resumes only after a human decision.
ai.quote: Reads run immediately. Writes wait for a person.

gate.illustrative: An illustrative replay of the copilot screen below. The proposal, its fields and its reason are copied from that screen; the timing is not. Record content stays in English, as it does in the app.

risk.d: Every tool is classed by its consequence, not by its name.
risk.note: Bulk approval is offered only for low and medium risk. Proposals expire after 72 hours by default.

screens.approval: Copilot paused on a proposed stage change
screens.actions: AI Action Center with risk labels and expiry
screens.inbox: AI Inbox, filled by the hourly proactive scanner

ai.disclosure: The copilot screens use the project’s deterministic Fake model driver, the same approach as its end-to-end tests. Only the model’s choice of tool calls was scripted. Tool execution, policy checks, risk classification, proposal creation and the run pause are the real application code. No live model call was made.

Organisation scoping, plus validation rules that reject a reference to another tenant’s records.
Roles per organisation and Laravel policies, with tests that keep the API and the interface in parity.
An SSRF-safe fetcher: public addresses only, the connection pinned to the validated address, and every redirect checked again.

crma.architecture: A modular Laravel 12 monolith serving an Inertia and React 19 app, a versioned REST API, an AI API and an MCP server. MySQL 8 and Redis 7 with Horizon queues, Reverb WebSockets and a scheduler, packaged as Docker Compose services and shipped through GitHub Actions.

AI writes stored as proposals with a 72-hour expiry, executed only after approval (ActionEngine).
Hybrid retrieval: lexical and vector results fused with RRF, filtered by organization.
An MCP server behind OAuth, exposing read and propose tools to external agents.
Organization-scoped data with tenant-isolation tests.

restocafe.title: RestoCafe OS
restocafe.lede: A multi-branch restaurant platform built around one hard problem: keeping an order correct while tills, a kitchen screen and a patchy connection all touch it.

facts.v: Restaurant POS, kitchen and table service
NestJS API, Prisma schema, ops PWA

restocafe.problem: A waiter adds a dish while the cashier splits the bill and the kitchen marks it ready. Every one of them must see the same order, and none of them may overwrite the others.
restocafe.flowIntro: The order moves through explicit states. Each transition is checked on the server and broadcast to every screen that shows it.

flow.d: Items added at the table or the till.
Sent to the kitchen; the order is now shared.
The kitchen board picks it up in real time.
Marked from the kitchen; the floor is notified.

decisions.d: A retried request with the same key returns the first result instead of applying twice.
Updates carry the version they were based on; a stale write is rejected, not merged.
Seating and moving orders between tables runs under SELECT … FOR UPDATE.
The ops app queues actions while offline and replays them on reconnect, with tests for the queue.
Socket.IO with a Redis adapter, and a short-lived socket token instead of the session cookie.

restocafe.screensNote: Captured by the repository’s own Playwright visual tests against a seeded local build. Orders, tables and amounts are test data.
verified: NestJS, Prisma and PostgreSQL, with a schema of around forty models.
An idempotency-key store and version checks (expectedVersion) on order updates.
Row locking in the table service.
Socket.IO with a Redis adapter and a dedicated socket token.
An offline queue in the ops web app, with its own tests.
notClaimed: It is not deployed and has no restaurants using it.
k6 load scripts and Kubernetes manifests exist, but no load results or production cluster are claimed.
The history is short: most of the work is still uncommitted.
restocafe.tests: Executed on 18 Oct 2026 against the working tree: 112 passed, 6 failed, 3 skipped (Jest, 2 of 33 suites failing, including the order-lifecycle suite).
restocafe.architecture: A NestJS and TypeScript API with Prisma on PostgreSQL, Redis for the Socket.IO adapter and caching, and a React PWA for operations with an offline queue.

mtjri.title: Mtjri
mtjri.lede: Multi-store commerce where AI drafts each store’s landing content in the background, and a validator decides whether it is fit to save.

facts.v: Store builder, back office, POS and storefront
Laravel, Inertia and React, queued jobs

mtjri.flowIntro: Generating a store’s content is a job, not a request.

flow.d: A job is dispatched for the store.
The provider manager calls a model.
The output is checked against rules.

decisions.d: Whole-store generation and single-section regeneration run as separate queued jobs.
Ollama by default, with an optional OpenAI fallback behind one interface.
Generated landing content must pass a validator before it reaches the store.
AI models belong to a store through a shared trait, so one store never reads another’s drafts.

mtjri.screensNote: The platform admin, a store’s back office and its storefront, from a local build with demo stores and orders.
verified: Queued jobs for store and section generation.
A provider manager with Ollama and an optional OpenAI fallback.
A validator for generated landing content, and store-scoped AI models.
Around three dozen test files in the repository (not run for this page).
notClaimed: The source arrived in a single commit, so the history does not show how it was built.
It is not deployed and has no merchants.
Generation quality has not been measured.
mtjri.architecture: Laravel with Inertia and React, queued jobs for AI generation, an AI provider manager over Ollama and OpenAI, and store-scoped models.

Deals, contacts, leads, tasks and a typed workflow engine
A bounded, model-directed tool loop with step and call budgets
AI writes become proposals that expire unless a person approves
Hybrid lexical and vector search, filtered by organization

about.heading: About.
body: I am a backend engineer who starts with the business: how a sale is approved, how a booking is held, how money is split. The code comes after the operation is clear.
Most of my work is Laravel, FastAPI and NestJS on relational databases, with the AI layer built as part of the system rather than beside it.

rakez.lede: An ERP built for a Saudi real-estate company: sales, reservations, contracts, commissions and marketing in one Arabic-first platform, built with a small team.

items.d: A waiting list and row locks for contested units
Commission and distribution records with project policies
Role-based access checked on the server
Meta, Google and TikTok leads mapped to their project
OpenAI-backed answers in Arabic for the sales team
